data.body:
═══ FIX LANDED IN WORKTREE (branch fix/afeb-class-bypass) — four sites now select from the class
vocabulary, plus a GENERAL provenance guard so a fifth cannot appear silently ═══

**RED first, confirmed.** New file `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`. Before any source
change all six per-site probes failed with the discriminating string, e.g.
`assert 'anthropic:cfg-model-must-not-be-inherited' == 'test:standard-class-model'` — i.e. the site
ran cfg.model while a class table was configured. That is exactly the ticket's config B, expressed
offline: the class table is patched at `llm.config._read_llm_file_table` (the one function
`load_class_slots` reads) with all three classes pointed at sentinels DISTINCT from cfg.model, so
"honoured the class" and "fell through to cfg.model" are different strings rather than the same one.

**MUTATION CHECK (the test has teeth).** With the fix in place I re-introduced the exact root cause
at all four sites (replaced each binding with `pass`) and re-ran: 8 tests returned to RED — the six
probes and both guards. Restored, 12/12 green.

**THE FOUR CLASS CHOICES, each decided on the PROMPT's shape (execution_mode + tools +
open-endedness), not on "it's a sub-call". This reasoning is the durable part and is written into
each site as a comment:**

    site                                  class      why
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    llm/enrich.py (ticket-digest)         trivial    single_turn, NO tools, "Not a reviewer";
                                                     extracts four constrained fields from given
                                                     text. Narrow canonicalizing work — and the
                                                     highest-VOLUME site (store write path), so the
                                                     cheapest win of the four.
    llm/overlap/judge.py (overlap-judge)  standard   single_turn, tool-less, but picks ONE relation
                                                     from a closed 5-value set and must cite a named
                                                     shared artifact while "false flags are costly".
                                                     Precision-sensitive JUDGEMENT = the operator's
                                                     default. NOT frontier: 18 of 23 calls.
    code_review/workflow_ops.py           standard   IS a code-review pass (category
      (code-novelty)                                 `code-review-pass`, factual tri-state match), so
                                                     the Pass-2/Pass-4 rule applies directly. This
                                                     also makes the docstring's claimed parity with
                                                     plan-review's `_score_floor_novelty` (which runs
                                                     `_verifier_cfg` = standard) TRUE; it was false.
    llm/operations.py (ticket-quality)    frontier   NOT standard. This is `rebar review`'s default
                                                     reviewer: `execution_mode: agentic`, category
                                                     `review`, WITH file + MCP tools, told to inspect
                                                     the code paths a ticket references. An
                                                     open-ended FINDER (Pass-1 analogue); the
                                                     standard rule covers verification passes.

Fix shape at every site: `cfg = replace(cfg, model=resolve_model_string(<CLASS>))`, the same
mechanism `_verifier_cfg` and the completion verifier already use. Placed INSIDE the existing
try/except at the two fail-safe sites, so a config error is still an abstain (overlap stays advisory
and never blocks) / still yields `{}` (novelty degrades to keeping MORE findings). Both fail-safes
have their own tests in the new file.

`ticket-digest` is bound INSIDE `enrich()` rather than at its callers, deliberately: the store write
path (`enrich_drain.drain` → `enrich`) builds its own config from the environment and passes none in,
so a caller-side fix would have missed exactly the path that matters most. There is a probe for that
`config=None` route.

**THE GENERAL GUARD — a provenance analysis, not a list of today's four.**
`test_no_run_request_inherits_the_raw_config_model` walks the AST of every `.py` in `src/rebar`,
finds every `RunRequest(...)`, and traces its `config=` expression backwards: a class binder
(`resolve_model_string`/`resolve_model`/`_verifier_cfg`/…) anywhere in the chain cleanses it, a bare
`LLMConfig.from_env` at the end of it is the defect, and a PARAMETER transfers the obligation to
that function's callers across the whole package (which is how it reaches `judge_one` through
`judge()`). Verdicts are bound / raw / unresolved. Pre-fix it reported
`enrich`, `review_ticket`, `judge_one` as raw and `score_code_novelty` as an unregistered
unfollowable site — i.e. it flagged all four WITHOUT naming any of them.

Two small registries carry the sites the rule cannot pass on its own, each entry with a written
reason, and both are staleness-checked so an entry cannot rot into a licence:
 * `_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN` — exactly ONE entry: `spec_scan._scan_epics_inner`. It is a top-level op's
   PRIMARY call (not a sub-call), and it is the one site the ticket's measurement could not exercise
   (needs `--spec-file`), so afeb scopes it out rather than change it unmeasured. **Flagging this
   for the operator**: if `scan-spec` should also move onto the class vocabulary, that is a separate
   one-line change — I did not make it, both because it is out of this ticket's measured scope and
   because `src/rebar/llm/spec_scan.py` was outside my file budget for this parallel run.
 * `_UNFOLLOWABLE` — 7 entries the analysis stops at (attribute configs like
   `completion_recovery`'s `self._config`; params whose binding happens through call chains it does
   not follow: `passes.pass1_chunk`, `passes.pass4_coach`, `prerequisites.run_focused_finder`; and
   three eval harnesses that pin cfg.model as their control).

Also asserted: the scan itself finds ≥15 sites and every site passes SOME config, so the guard
cannot pass vacuously if `RunRequest` construction ever moves behind a factory.

**One deliberate weakening of the analysis, recorded rather than hidden**: when a name has several
assignments, `bound` wins over `raw`. That is required for the rebind shape the fix itself uses
(`cfg = replace(cfg, model=resolve_model_string(...))`) and for the workflow engine's own
`RunnerAgentStep`, which mints from `from_env` then rebinds via `resolve_model`. The cost: a function
that binds a class for one call and passes the raw config to a SECOND RunRequest would read as bound.
The per-site probes cover the places where that would currently matter.

Gates: `make lint` clean, `make typecheck` clean (mypy, 407 files). All four touched src files stay
well under the 800-line cap (largest: workflow_ops.py at 691). Targeted suites green: the new file,
enrich/enrich_drain/enrich_queue/overlap_judge/overlap_retrieve/plan_review_overlap/
ticket_digest_store/model_classes (128 passed, 1 skipped), and tests/unit/workflow +
code_review region-gate/per-pass-classes/verifier-class (539 passed).

**NOT done / for the reviewer:** `docs/env-vars.md` was not regenerated (no env-var surface changed).
`llm/overlap/wire.py` needed no change — binding inside `judge_one` covers every route into it.
